text:
Maria L: FYI customer 'FinEdge' hit a hard block: private control plane can't egress to eu-west-3 for the fallback path, so SmartRouter couldn't route to hosted fallback. Customer's egress whitelist is very strict.

Kevin H: ugh. did the control plane try the regional mirror first or straight to global fallback?

Maria L: regional mirror (eu-west-3) failed DNS/connect. then router attempted fallback to hosted-us-east as configured by policy, but our egress was blocked by customer's firewall.

Anika S: this is a product/UX problem — console shows "fallback succeeded" when it actually queued and then failed due to egress deny. we need clearer states: attempted->blocked-by-egress->awaiting-customer-action. :warning:

Samir R: on the infra side, we currently assume control plane egress to all supported regions for fallbacks. For Private customers we should respect the customer's allowed-regions list and not auto-route outside it unless explicitly permitted.

Kevin H: agree. also internal API debate: should SmartRouter return 4xx to the client when all fallbacks are outside allowed regions, or should it return 5xx and mark as retryable?

Julia P: From SLA perspective, 5xx with retry isn't great if customer intentionally blocked egress. 4xx with a clear error code (e.g., `private_egress_blocked`) is better for them to handle.

Maria L: +1 on explicit error code. Console should surface the exact blocked target (region + model variant).

Samir R: implementation idea: add `allowed_regions` check into the routing policy stage. Pseudocode:
```
if request.customer.allowed_regions does not contain candidate_region:
    mark candidate as "egress_forbidden"
    skip to next candidate
```
We also need telemetry events for `egress_forbidden` with tags: customer_id, attempted_region, model_id, tier.

Anika S: and the rollout dashboard needs a new column for "egress constraints" so SRE and customer success can see how many requests are failing due to egress rather than model quality.

Kevin H: telemetry naming: prefer `router.egress.blocked` and `router.fallback.attempt` with attribute `decision=skipped_by_policy`. keeps it consistent with existing `router.*` metrics.

Maria L: ops-bot created ticket: INF-4921. please add test cases. We should also allow an override flag for on-prem admin (`allow_out_of_region_fallback`) that requires an explicit signed consent and shows a big warning in Console.

ops-bot: INF-4921 created by Maria L — "Private routing: respect customer's allowed_regions and surface egress-blocks in console/telemetry". Priority: P1. Assignees: Samir R, Anika S.

Samir R: question — for model-variant fallback (eg quantized smaller variant hosted in different region), do we treat model_variant.region the same as region? i.e., if variant A is in us-east and is outside allowed regions, skip it?

Julia P: yes, region constraints apply to the endpoint that would be contacted. If the variant's serving endpoint is outside allowed regions, it's blocked. But we can propose local variant switching (swap to quantized variant deployed within customer's allowed region) as an alternative when available.

Anika S: UX note: in rollout canary UI add a tooltip: "Requests blocked by egress settings won't be counted toward canary success rate". customer confusion is currently our #1 support ping on this.

Kevin H: API change: add `X-Redwood-Route-Decision` header on responses when a fallback was considered but skipped due to egress rule, value `skipped_by_egress`. That helps downstream infra and customers to debug.

Maria L: Samir / Kevin please sync on telemetry + header names and drop a short RFC in the eng-platform RFC channel. We need a staging plan: simulate blocked egress with iptables in Private env and run load tests.

Samir R: will do. plan: 1) add allowed_regions gating in SmartRouter; 2) emit `router.egress.blocked` metric + logs; 3) header `X-Redwood-Route-Decision`; 4) console state update + tooltip; 5) feature-flagged rollout.

Maria L: thanks. tagging @anika to update console mocks and @cs-team for customer comms.

Julia P: small note: quotas — if we skip fallback, do we refund token usage? needs policy.

Kevin H: we currently don't charge for failed attempts after handshake. But for skipped_by_egress we should ensure no token billing occurs and log `billing.zero_charge_reason=egress_block`.

Maria L: good catch. add billing tag to ticket.

Anika S: I'll mock the UI states today. Samir please add telemetry to the staging branch so I can wire the dashboard.

Samir R: on it. I'll also add an integration test that asserts `router.egress.blocked` increments when allowed_regions excludes the chosen region.

Maria L: great. we'll review RFC tomorrow in standup. :thumbsup:
